summary: You run a Scottish clan building a production network that turns raw grain, wool, and wood into higher-value whisky, cloth, and tools, selling on a price-sensitive market or fulfilling exclusive contracts. It plays as a tight five-round optimization puzzle where efficient conversion chains and timing your sales matter far more than fighting over the board.
praised: market prices that realistically swing with supply and demand
strong variable player powers (clans) and solo mode
scales well and rewards efficient planning
criticised: thin, pasted-on theme over a spreadsheet-like engine
can feel like multiplayer solitaire with little direct interaction
dense iconography and rules overhead for new players
early missteps are hard to recover from in only 5 rounds

interaction.kind: shared market pressure and contract racing
interaction.detail: Players mostly build and run separate production networks on their own boards, so most of the game is parallel, but selling goods depresses that good's price for everyone and exclusive contracts/land tiles can be claimed out from under you.

scoring.how_you_win: After exactly 5 rounds, whoever has accumulated the most points from money, goods, buildings, and bonus objectives wins.
